title: Control Measures for Drug Abuse and Addiction

headings.title: Introduction to Drug Abuse and Addiction
headings.content:
Drug abuse involves the patterned use of a substance in which the user consumes the substance in amounts or with methods neither approved nor supervised by medical professionals. **Substance dependence**, often referred to clinically as addiction, represents a chronic, relapsing brain disease characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use, despite harmful consequences. It fundamentally alters brain structure and chemistry, specifically targeting the reward circuitry regulated by dopamine.

In clinical settings across Nigeria, understanding this distinction prevents moralizing patient care. Addiction is a health condition requiring structured intervention, not a failure of willpower.

headings.title: Primary Prevention and Public Health Education
headings.content:
Primary prevention focuses on stopping drug abuse before it ever starts. Public health initiatives aim to build personal and community resilience against substance use through targeted awareness campaigns.

- **School-based programs**: Educating adolescents about physiological and social consequences of psychoactive substances before experimentation occurs.
- **Community outreach**: Town hall meetings and media campaigns addressing local drug trends, such as codeine or tramadol misuse in Nigerian communities.
- **Peer-led initiatives**: Empowering youth ambassadors who can effectively counter peer pressure within social networks.

Targeted education addresses the specific local vulnerabilities of a population, reducing the incidence of first-time drug use.

headings.title: Screening and Early Identification Techniques
headings.content:
Early identification prevents mild substance involvement from progressing into severe dependence. Healthcare facilities utilize structured screening tools during routine patient assessments.

Commonly applied screening instruments include:
- **CAGE Questionnaire**: A brief four-question tool evaluating Cut down, Annoyed, Guilt, and Eye-opener behaviors regarding alcohol.
- **AUDIT**: The Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test developed by the World Health Organization for hazardous drinking patterns.
- **ASSIST**: The Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test, which covers multiple classes of psychoactive substances.

Observing subtle behavioral cues—such as unexplained chronic fatigue, sudden financial distress, or frequent absenteeism—assists nurses in recognizing unreported substance use.

headings.title: Pharmacological and Non-Pharmacological Management
headings.content:
Managing substance addiction requires a dual approach combining medical stabilization with behavioral modification.

| Approach Category | Primary Methods | Clinical Goal |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pharmacological** | Agonist therapy, antagonist medications, symptom-relief drugs | Safely manage withdrawal and reduce intense cravings |
| **Non-Pharmacological** | Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, counseling, support groups | Modify behavioral triggers and maintain long-term sobriety |

Medical stabilization during acute withdrawal must be monitored carefully, as abrupt cessation of certain substances like alcohol or sedatives can trigger life-threatening complications such as delirium tremens.

headings.title: Legal, Ethical, and Regulatory Frameworks in Nigeria
headings.content:
Control measures rely heavily on statutory laws and regulatory bodies. In Nigeria, the **National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)** leads the fight against cultivation, production, trafficking, and abuse of illicit substances. Additionally, the **National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)** regulates the manufacture, importation, and distribution of legitimate pharmaceuticals to prevent diversion into illicit markets.

Nurses must navigate these frameworks ethically, balancing legal obligations to report illegal acts with the professional duty of patient confidentiality and therapeutic trust.

headings.title: The Role of the Nurse in Substance Abuse Control
headings.content:
Nurses occupy a frontline position across community health centers, psychiatric units, and general medical wards. Core responsibilities include conducting objective health assessments, administering prescribed withdrawal medications, and delivering psychoeducation without prejudice.

Creating a therapeutic environment allows patients to disclose substance use habits honestly without fear of criminal prosecution by hospital staff. Advocacy for rehabilitation resources within local health systems remains an essential nursing duty.
